title: The proper projection formula on the ambient category
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $r:V\to T$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of finite type between Noetherian schemes (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Work on the small etale sites and in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(V_{\Et},A)$ and $D(T_{\Et},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Write $r^*=r^{-1}$ for the termwise exact inverse image of constant-coefficient module sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $Rr_*$ for its derived right adjoint. For every $L\in D(V_{\Et},A)$ and $K\in D(T_{\Et},A)$, the canonical derived tensor projection map
$$
K\otimes_A^L Rr_*L\longrightarrow Rr_*(r^*K\otimes_A^L L)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(T_{\Et},A)$. Precisely, this map is the composite
$$
K\otimes_A^L Rr_*L
\xrightarrow{\sigma}Rr_*L\otimes_A^L K
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_r(L,K)}Rr_*(L\otimes_A^L r^{-1}K)
\xrightarrow{Rr_*(\sigma)}Rr_*(r^{-1}K\otimes_A^L L),
$$
where $\mathrm{PF}$ is the adjoint-of-counit map of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $\sigma$ is the canonical derived tensor symmetry of [lem-kun-tensor-sym], represented by the sign $(-1)^{pq}$ swap on K-flat complexes in bidegree $(p,q)$. No boundedness, constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, pro-etale completion, or invertibility of $|A|$ on the schemes is assumed.

proof.text: Because $A$ is finite, two multiples $i1_A,j1_A$ with $0\le i<j$ coincide, and subtraction gives $(j-i)1_A=0$. Multiplication by any $a\in A$ shows $(j-i)a=0$, so $A$ is a torsion ring, including the zero ring. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], inverse image of constant-coefficient module sheaves is exact and agrees with module pullback. Termwise inverse image therefore preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms: kernels, images and their quotients are preserved by exactness. It gives $r^*=r^{-1}$ on the unbounded derived categories, with no resolution or boundedness restriction on $K$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0f0g] with $f=r$, $X=V$, $Y=T$, $\Lambda=A$, $E=L$, and the given $K$. Its hypotheses are properness, the torsion-ring condition proved in Step 1, and membership in the two unbounded small-etale derived categories; all hold. It makes the specified canonical map $\mathrm{PF}_r(L,K):Rr_*L\otimes_A^L K\to Rr_*(L\otimes_A^L r^{-1}K)$ an isomorphism. The theorem imposes no boundedness or Tor-amplitude condition and does not require a uniform cohomological-dimension bound over $T$. The additional Noetherian and finite-type hypotheses of this item are harmless.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-tensor-sym] on $T$ to $(K,Rr_*L)$ and on $V$ to $(L,r^{-1}K)$, with coefficient ring $A$. It gives the canonical derived isomorphisms $s:K\otimes_A^LRr_*L\to Rr_*L\otimes_A^LK$ and $t:L\otimes_A^Lr^{-1}K\to r^{-1}K\otimes_A^LL$. These are the symmetries specified in the statement; [def-kun-derived-tensor] fixes the signed swap underlying the canonical symmetry. If $t^{-1}$ is the inverse, functoriality gives $Rr_*(t^{-1})Rr_*(t)=1$ and $Rr_*(t)Rr_*(t^{-1})=1$. Put $p=\mathrm{PF}_r(L,K)$, the adjoint-of-counit map of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], invertible by Step 2. The ordered projection map is exactly $Rr_*(t)\circ p\circ s$ by the displayed definition in the statement. Its inverse is $s^{-1}\circ p^{-1}\circ Rr_*(t^{-1})$: the two composites cancel adjacent inverse pairs. Hence the claimed map is an isomorphism.
